summary.headline: Kajaria Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR 1,373 crore with volume up 11% and EBITDA margin at 19.19% versus 10.01% a year ago.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 12% YoY to INR 1,373 crore, with tiles volume up 11%, helped by sales-channel unification and a Morbi shutdown that cut industry supply. EBITDA margin expanded to 19.19% from 10.01%, and PAT rose to INR 136 crore from INR 43 crore. Production fell about 7% in the quarter as Morbi plants shut in March, and inventory was drawn down by roughly 1.5 million square meters. Management says all plants, including Morbi, have run at full capacity since 16 April, but outsourcing from Morbi remains uncertain. Management declined to give volume guidance and said it expects margins of 18% to 19%.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give volume guidance, citing past guidance that did not materialise; it said it will not give volume numbers going forward.
EBITDA margin expected to be maintained between 18% and 19% under the current scenario.
Price increases of about 12% to 13% in North and about 15% to 17% in Morbi and South (Q4 gas-linked); further price increase effective 1 April. Realisation gains may be partly offset by discounts.
Q1 is seasonally weak; management said full-year FY27 will be much better, but would not split quarters.
Ad spend in FY27 expected to be 40% to 50% higher than FY26 (FY26 ad spend about INR 90 to 100 crore).
Promoter salaries not to be taken in FY27; some employee salary action under consideration.
Outsourcing from Morbi expected to be about 40 million square meters in FY27 versus about 32 million (or 22 million per another remark) in FY26; supply disruption expected for one to two months.
capex_capacity: Production fell about 7% in Q4 FY26 due to Morbi plant shutdown in March; Morbi plants restarted 16 April 2026 and all Kajaria plants, including Morbi, are said to be running at full capacity.
Company-owned and JV capacity produced about 87 million square meters in FY26 against 118 million square meters of sales; outsourcing supplied about 32 million square meters.
Outsourcing reported at about 27% to 28% of material sourced from Morbi currently; management expects this to be disrupted in April and May.
Inventory about 11 million square meters, after falling about 1.5 million square meters in March.
Biofuel makes up about 30% of fuel mix in North plants (one remark said about 15% company-wide); biofuel cost about INR 20 per SCM in North, used only in spray dryers.
Buyback decision cited cash on balance sheet well above capex needs; buyback is more tax-efficient for shareholders from this point, and expected to improve ROE.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is good; tiles are a small share of construction cost, so the price increase is not expected to stop construction.
Morbi gas cost rose sharply; management said the landed gas price moved from about INR 47 to 50 per SCM to about INR 84 today, implying a 35% to 40% cost increase for Morbi players.
Kajaria's Q4 average gas cost per SCM: North INR 55.54, South INR 49.6, West INR 46.57. April: North about INR 62.5, South about INR 81, West about INR 79.

Management estimates only 150 to 160 Morbi plants will run from 1 May, versus 500 to 600 plants in the industry; competitors are reportedly clearing stock, which management sees as favourable for organised players.
Exports from Morbi were about INR 400 to 500 crore in April, with Gulf freight rates up sharply (UAE freight about $4,000 versus $300 before the conflict).
Propane supply to industry has been halted by a government circular dated 5 March, so Morbi relies on gas; government priority is domestic LPG, then fertiliser, then power, then industry.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 volume growth came from the Morbi shutdown, and how is Q1 looking?
qa_highlights.answer: Chetan Kajaria said growth was not only due to Morbi, with January and February volume up 8% to 9%. Management would not split quarterly numbers but said the momentum has started. Sanjeev Agarwal said Q1 is historically weak and full-year FY27 will be much better.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes were taken and how do gas costs compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases of about 12% to 13% in North and 16% to 17% in Morbi and South, effective early March. Management said the hikes cover the gas cost increase with some margin. Further prices rose 1 April, and realisations may be partly offset by discounts.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 12% to 15% price increase fully reflect in Q1 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Rishi Kajaria said some realisation increase is definite. Sanjeev Agarwal said it cannot be quantified because the situation is dynamic and some discounts may be given.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and dependence on Morbi outsourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: All plants are running at full capacity from 16 April. Outsourcing from Morbi is about 27% to 28% of material currently, and this is a question mark for April and May. Management expects a one to two month disruption, with outsourcing rising to about 40 million square meters in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will Morbi competition increase domestically when plants restart?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Kajaria said only about 70 to 90 Morbi plants were running, with an expected 150 to 160 from 1 May. Management said the domestic market is short of supply and that Morbi players have sold out their stock, which benefits multi-location organised players.

qa_highlights.question: What are cost trends and the margin outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Kajaria said some cost increase is expected but will be offset by volume growth and the 1 April price increase. Sanjeev Agarwal said absolute staff costs may rise, but administrative costs as a percentage of sales will fall. Margin is expected at 18% to 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gas cost in North lower than in South and West?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GAIL is the nodal agency for pipeline gas under a government formula that gives 80% at normal prices and 20% at spot prices for North plants. South plants paid spot prices in April and moved to normal prices from 1 May.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ad spend and salary plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 ad spend was about INR 90 to 100 crore; FY27 spend expected 40% to 50% higher with a new TVC. Management said promoter salaries will not be taken in FY26 or in FY27.

risks_watch: Morbi restart pace after 1 May and the share of outsourced supply that returns (outsourcing was about 27% to 28% of material in April).
Gas supply and price volatility: the government formula (80% normal, 20% spot) and Morbi landed gas cost of about INR 84 per SCM.
Whether competitors pass on the 35% to 40% gas-driven cost increase, and whether price discounts erode the 12% to 17% price hikes.
Propane availability for industry, and whether the government changes the policy.
Gulf export disruption from high freight rates, which may push Morbi supply into the domestic market.
Sustainability of the 19.19% EBITDA margin versus management's 18% to 19% guide, as costs and ad spend rise.
Management has withheld volume guidance; the company has earlier missed its own volume guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and margins but cautious and evasive on near-term specifics; management declined quarterly and volume guidance and repeatedly said Morbi supply is unknown. Its answers on gas formulas and pricing were detailed and direct.
key_quotes: So my request will be going forward not to give any guidance, and we perform and prove to you people that we are doing a good job as a team.
Margin, we are confident that with the current scenario, we should be maintaining between 18% to 19%.
The journey has just begun, and we remain optimistic about the current year's performance and beyond.
So we have decided not to give any volume guidance, number one.

growth.why: No volume guidance given (dropped); only EBITDA margin guided at 18-19% under current scenario, with price hikes of 12-17% and Morbi disruption as backing, but no concrete capacity additions or orders, so growth outlook is flat-to-unclear.
